title: ‘HalluSquatting’ Turns AI Hallucinations Into Botnet Delivery Mechanism - SecurityWeek
body: **Researchers from Tel Aviv University, Technion, and Intuit have detailed a new attack technique dubbed ‘HalluSquatting’ that turns AI assistants’ tendency to hallucinate into a scalable infection vector.**. These promptware attacks leverage the fact that the attacker has a direct channel to the targeted user’s LLM application. HalluSquatting, on the other hand, has been described as a form of untargeted promptware that relies on a technique named adversarial hallucination squatting, in which threat actors can exploit AI applications at scale without a direct channel. In a HalluSquatting attack, the attacker pre-registers the fake repository or package names that LLMs commonly invent when asked to fetch popular, trending resources. The HalluSquatting research has focused on using the technique to create agentic botnets whose size depends on how often AI tools hallucinate the attacker’s squatted resource. title: Encrypted Prompts Bypass AI Safety Guardrails in Grok and Gemini - SecurityWeek
body: # Encrypted Prompts Bypass AI Safety Guardrails in Grok and Gemini. Researchers say the new ‘Cryptographic Context Injection’ technique conceals malicious instructions until they are decrypted inside a trusted execution environment. **Researchers at Adversa AI discovered a new attack technique and named it Cryptographic Context Injection. The result is the plaintext prompt is recovered inside the trusted execution context and not flagged by the guardrails as harmful. The decrypted prompt could instruct the model, “to reach out to external servers, leaking the user’s data through request parameters, or produce some other undesired output and re-encrypt it to smuggle it past output guardrails.” In an agentic scenario the instructions could instigate misuse of any tool available to the model. Through a series of tricks described by the researchers, the decrypted prompt can instruct the model to produce restricted content “framed as something it will encrypt ‘for safety’”. title: AI Coding Tools Tricked Into Hacking Developer Machine via Decades-Old Technique - SecurityWeek
body: Wiz has disclosed the details of a new AI coding assistant attack method it has dubbed GhostApproval. **Several popular AI coding assistants were tricked into facilitating developer machine hacking via an attack technique that has been known for decades, according to Google-owned cloud security giant Wiz.**. Dubbed **GhostApproval**, the attack has been successfully tested against Claude Code, Amazon Q Developer, Cursor, Google Antigravity, Augment, and Windsurf. The symlink vulnerability has been known since early Unix days, and Wiz researchers have now demonstrated that it’s exploitable against AI coding assistants. When a developer opens the repo in an AI coding assistant and instructs it to make edits, the agent follows the symlink and performs the write on the target specified by the attacker. Augment and Windsurf have confirmed receipt of the vulnerability reports but have yet to release fixes, according to Wiz. The cybersecurity company on Wednesday published technical details for the GhostApproval vulnerability. body: # The election that will shape the future of AI. **Whether they fully appreciate it or not, Californians will be deciding on the future of global AI regulation** when they head to the voting booths on Tuesday. AI is a hot button issue across the world, but much of the national and international policy governing the technology still begins in California, where the most advanced AI labs are headquartered.
